title: SIFT (The Four Moves) (Mike Caulfield, 19 June 2019)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The four moves: Stop; Investigate the source; Find better coverage; Trace claims, quotes and media to the original context. Quick checks for everyday claims, deeper checks for claims that matter.

title: Evaluating Information: Applying the CRAAP Test (17 September 2010)
publisher: Meriam Library, California State University, Chico
supports: Opened with WebFetch (PDF text extracted). The checklist's five criteria: Currency, Relevance, Authority, Accuracy and Purpose, each with question prompts; the library notes criteria matter more or less depending on the need.

title: Civic Online Reasoning
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Free lessons built from observing professional fact checkers, who ask three questions: who is behind the information, what is the evidence, and what do other sources say. Lists an Intro to Lateral Reading lesson.

title: The commitments of the IFCN Code of Principles
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Five commitments: non-partisanship and fairness; transparency of sources (enough detail to replicate); transparency of funding and organisation; transparency of methodology; an open and honest corrections policy.

title: Full Fact toolkit
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Three questions for any claim: where is it from, what is missing, how do you feel; links to guides on AI-generated images, deepfake videos, misleading footage and poll figures.

title: Fabrication and errors in the bibliographic citations generated by ChatGPT (Walters and Wilder, Scientific Reports 13:14045, 7 September 2023)
publisher: PubMed Central (US National Library of Medicine)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 42 topics, 84 short reviews, 636 citations: 55% of GPT-3.5 and 18% of GPT-4 citations were fabricated; 43% and 24% of the real ones had substantive errors (volume, issue, pages and years most often). Advice: check every citation in a database and do not ask the chatbot to verify its own references.

title: News: Crossref and Retraction Watch (12 September 2023, updated 10 October 2024)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Crossref acquired the Retraction Watch database and made it a public resource; about 43k Retraction Watch entries and 14k Crossref entries, around 50k combined; data released through the Labs API and, from October 2024, a GitLab repository.

title: Retraction Watch data (documentation, last updated 19 January 2025)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Retractions appear in a work's update-to field in the REST API (source publisher or retraction-watch); the CSV is updated each working day; notice types include retraction, correction, expression of concern and reinstatement; coverage is not complete.

title: The Retraction Watch Hijacked Journal Checker
supports: Opened with WebFetch. A spreadsheet, built with Anna Abalkina, of journals suspected of being hijacked; hijacked journals copy a real journal's title, ISSN and other metadata without permission.

title: Think. Check. Submit.
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Checklists for judging whether a journal or book publisher is trustworthy, led by representatives of ALPSP, AUP, COPE, DOAJ, ISSN, LIBER, OAPEN, OASPA, STM and UKSG.

title: Why Most Published Research Findings Are False (John P. A. Ioannidis, 30 August 2005)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Corollaries: a finding is less likely to be true when studies are small, effects are small, many relationships are tested with little preselection, designs and analyses are flexible, financial or other interests are present, and the field is crowded and hot.

title: American Statistical Association releases statement on statistical significance and p-values (7 March 2016)
supports: Opened with WebFetch (PDF text extracted). Six principles: p-values can show incompatibility with a model; they do not measure the probability that a hypothesis is true or that chance alone produced the data; decisions should not rest only on a threshold; full reporting is needed; a p-value does not measure effect size or importance; alone it is not a good measure of evidence.

title: GRADE Working Group
supports: Opened with WebFetch. A transparent system, begun in 2000, for rating certainty of evidence (high, moderate, low, very low) per outcome; domains include risk of bias, imprecision, inconsistency, indirectness, publication bias, large effects, dose-response and plausible opposing bias.

title: Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions, current version (version 6.5, 2024)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Current version 6.5 (2024); chapter 4 covers searching for and selecting studies, chapter 8 risk of bias in randomised trials (RoB 2), chapter 15 interpreting results.

title: Cochrane Handbook, Chapter 15: Interpreting results and drawing conclusions (Schünemann and others)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. A fall from 4% to 3% is a 25% relative but 1-point absolute reduction; present absolute effects as natural frequencies; report confidence intervals; an interval including no effect does not prove no effect; wording tied to certainty (reduces, probably, may, very uncertain); do not confuse no evidence of effect with evidence of no effect.

title: PRISMA 2020 statement
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Reporting guideline for systematic reviews: a checklist of items and sub-items, an expanded checklist, an abstract checklist and template flow diagrams for new and updated reviews (statement DOI 10.1136/bmj.n71).

title: EQUATOR Network
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Library of 700+ health research reporting guidelines; main ones by study type: CONSORT (trials), STROBE (observational), PRISMA (systematic reviews), STARD (diagnostic accuracy), COREQ (interviews and focus groups), SRQR (qualitative), CHEERS (economic evaluations).

title: What is a DOI?
supports: Opened with WebFetch. A DOI is a persistent identifier with a prefix and suffix (e.g. 10.1000/182) that resolves through doi.org to the object; persistence depends on the organisations behind it.

title: Citation Style Language
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Open-source language for formatting citations; a crowdsourced repository of more than 10,000 free styles, used by Zotero, Mendeley, Paperpile, RefWorks, pandoc and others.

title: The Chicago Manual of Style Online
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The current edition is the 18th (copyright 2024).

title: PubMed User Guide
supports: Opened with WebFetch. PubMed holds citations and abstracts, not full text; MeSH controlled vocabulary and [mh] tag; uppercase AND, OR, NOT with parentheses; filters by article type, date and more; Clipboard holds up to 500 items for 8 hours; email alerts need a My NCBI sign-in.

title: Google Scholar Search Help
supports: Opened with WebFetch. author: operator and quoted titles; Cited by and Related articles; email alerts; coverage not complete; record changes can take 6 to 12 months or longer; at most 1,000 results per query; no bulk access.

title: About Semantic Scholar
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Free AI-assisted search over 200 million+ academic papers from publisher partnerships, data providers and web crawls, with a public API and the Academic Graph dataset.

title: Using the Wayback Machine
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Browse captures of a URL by date (timestamp in the URL); Save Page Now saves one page; not every site is archived (robots.txt, passwords, exclusion requests); archived pages can be incomplete; new captures take 3 to 10 hours to appear.

title: Help with your research
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Research guides by subject, Discovery as the catalogue, guidance on citing records and reading old documents, free entry at Kew, paid search service or independent researchers.

title: Research Our Records
publisher: US National Archives and Records Administration
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The National Archives Catalog as the main search tool, with getting-started guides and research by topic.

title: Exceptions to copyright (updated 4 January 2021)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Fair dealing has no statutory definition; limited extracts for non-commercial research and private study with acknowledgement; quotation, criticism and review need sufficient acknowledgement; courts weigh market effect and whether the amount taken is necessary.

title: U.S. Copyright Office Fair Use Index
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Four factors: purpose and character, nature of the work, amount and substantiality, market effect; no set word count or percentage is always fair use.

title: Enabling and using web search
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Web search is switched on from the chat menu (Team and Enterprise need an owner to enable it); responses that use it include citations; in the newer Claude experience there is no toggle and Claude searches when it helps.
